identity.name: Sign-In Behavioral Anomaly on a Learned Identity Baseline — Cortex Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1078.004 / T1110.004)
identity.summary: A user whose learned Cortex sign-in profile is a stable set of ASNs, geographies and auth cadence is driven with stolen credentials — the identity tradecraft of Scattered Spider / Storm-0501. No single sign-in is a known-bad IOC; the deviation from the learned baseline (auth-velocity spike, new ASN, impossible travel) plus the causality chain is what an auto-tuned ABIOC fires on.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the user, endpoint, and network behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the IDENTITY (ITDR) plane against the learned per-user sign-in profile. It models the signature identity tradecraft attributed to Scattered Spider / Muddled Libra (UNC3944) and Storm-0501: after obtaining valid credentials (help-desk social engineering, SIM-swap, MFA fatigue, or purchased session material), the operator authenticates to the IdP from infrastructure that has never appeared in the victim's history. Cortex has learned that the target user signs in from a small, stable set of source ASNs and geographies at a human auth cadence — a handful of sessions per day from one or two corporate/home ISPs. The scenario injects three behavioral deviations from that learned baseline: (a) an auth-velocity spike — successful sign-ins at a rate and hour the account never exhibits; (b) a new-ASN deviation — a successful sign-in from an autonomous system (hosting/VPS or residential-proxy provider) absent from the learned profile; and (c) impossible travel — two successful sign-ins from geographically distant locations inside a travel-impossibility window. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific bad IP or a static geo-fence would miss this — the credentials are valid and each individual sign-in looks benign — which is exactly the point: the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the deviation from the account's learned sign-in behavior and anchors it to the causality chain (valid-account auth -> new-ASN/velocity deviation -> impossible-travel session pair). Two ABIOCs cover the deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL confirms the learned baseline and surfaces the anomalous session pair; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single account-takeover incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex's behavioral analytics caught a valid-credential intrusion no static rule was written for.

campaigns: Identity-driven account-takeover and hybrid-cloud intrusions against enterprise SaaS/IdP estates (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ITDR-009 — Sign-in behavioral deviation on a learned identity baseline for Cortex ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: An HTTP collector already wired into Cortex ITDR/XSIAM as a third-party IdP source so synthetic sign-in events reach okta_sso / msft_azure_ad_signin.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the target user signed in only from its normal ASNs and geographies so Cortex learned the per-identity sign-in profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad payloads. Drive a learned identity from off-baseline
# infrastructure and let the auth-velocity / new-ASN / impossible-travel
# deviation from the learned sign-in profile speak for itself.
set -euo pipefail
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/itdr-009.yml --live || true

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Authorised in-customer log collector wired into Cortex ITDR that receives the synthetic IdP sign-in events.

expected_artifacts.description: A successful sign-in for the target user from an autonomous system (ASN) that is absent from the account's learned sign-in baseline.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: auth_outcome = "SUCCESS" and src_asn not in learned_baseline_asns

expected_artifacts.description: Two successful sign-ins for the same user from geographically distant locations inside a travel-impossibility window.

abiocs.name: ITDR-009 Sign-In Auth-Velocity and New-ASN Deviation from Learned Identity Baseline
abiocs.description: A user whose learned Cortex sign-in profile is a narrow, stable set of source ASNs at a human auth cadence suddenly authenticates successfully from an autonomous system absent from the baseline, at a velocity the account never exhibits. Every credential is valid and no single IP is a known-bad IOC; the ABIOC fires on the ASN-and-velocity deviation from the account's learned behavior, anchored to the valid-account causality chain rather than to any static indicator.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter eventType = "user.session.start" and auth_outcome = "SUCCESS"
| comp count() as success_count, count_distinct(src_asn) as distinct_asns, values(src_asn) as asns, earliest(_time) as first_seen, latest(_time) as last_seen by actor_effective_username
| alter window_minutes = divide(subtract(last_seen, first_seen), 60000000)
| filter distinct_asns >= 2 and success_count >= 5 and window_minutes <= 60
| fields actor_effective_username, success_count, distinct_asns, asns, window_minutes, first_seen, last_seen
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-identity sign-in baseline (stable ASN set, human auth cadence) -> valid-account authentication from a new autonomous system at an anomalous velocity that diverges from the baseline, anchored to the originating auth event.

abiocs.name: ITDR-009 Impossible-Travel Geo-Velocity Deviation from Learned Sign-In Baseline
abiocs.description: The same user succeeds at two sign-ins from geographically distant locations inside a travel-impossibility window, deviating from the single-region geography Cortex learned for the account. The credentials are valid and each session in isolation is benign; the ABIOC fires on the geo-velocity deviation from the learned sign-in profile, anchored to the session pair spawned by the same stolen-credential intrusion.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter auth_outcome = "SUCCESS"
| comp count_distinct(src_geo_country) as geo_count, count_distinct(src_asn) as asn_count, values(src_geo_city) as cities, earliest(_time) as first_seen, latest(_time) as last_seen by user_name
| alter window_minutes = divide(subtract(last_seen, first_seen), 60000000)
| filter geo_count >= 2 and window_minutes <= 300
| sort desc geo_count
| fields user_name, geo_count, asn_count, cities, window_minutes, first_seen, last_seen
abiocs.causality_anchor: New-ASN valid-account auth -> a second successful session from a geographically distant location inside a travel-impossibility window that exceeds the account's learned single-region geography, anchored to the session pair from one intrusion.

xql_queries.name: ITDR-009 Learned Sign-In Baseline Present
xql_queries.query:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 604800)
| filter eventType = "user.session.start" and auth_outcome = "SUCCESS"
| comp count_distinct(src_asn) as baseline_asns, count_distinct(src_geo_country) as baseline_countries by actor_effective_username
| filter baseline_asns >= 1
| fields actor_effective_username, baseline_asns, baseline_countries

xql_queries.name: ITDR-009 Anomalous Session Pair Surfaced
xql_queries.query:
dataset = okta_sso
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter eventType = "user.session.start" and auth_outcome = "SUCCESS"
| comp count() as success_count, count_distinct(src_asn) as distinct_asns by actor_effective_username
| filter distinct_asns >= 2 and success_count >= 2
| fields actor_effective_username, success_count, distinct_asns

correlation_rules.name: Sign-In Account Takeover on a Learned Identity Baseline — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(ITDR-009 Sign-In Auth-Velocity and New-ASN Deviation from Learned Identity Baseline) AND ABIOC(ITDR-009 Impossible-Travel Geo-Velocity Deviation from Learned Sign-In Baseline) — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations on the same user into a single account-takeover incident anchored to the valid-account sign-in causality chain.

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM Analytics — auto-tuned behavioral profiling of per-identity sign-in ASN, geography and auth cadence

products.evidence_query: Two ABIOCs fire on the per-identity sign-in behavioral deviation; CR-ITDR-0008 stitches them into one account-takeover incident anchored to the valid-account causality chain.
dataset = okta_sso | filter auth_outcome = "SUCCESS" | comp count_distinct(src_asn) as distinct_asns by actor_effective_username | filter distinct_asns >= 2

use_cases.name: Sign-In Behavioral Anomaly Detection via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a user's sign-in baseline (ASN set, geography, auth cadence) and detect a valid-credential account takeover — auth-velocity spike, new ASN and impossible travel — anchored to its causality chain, where no static rule was written for the benign-looking individual sign-ins.

test_cases.objective: Cortex learns the target user's sign-in baseline and an injected off-baseline deviation fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: Collector wired into Cortex ITDR as a third-party IdP source.
Baseline window elapsed with the user signing in only from its normal ASNs/geos.
steps: Let the sign-in baseline window elapse.
Emit an auth-velocity/new-ASN burst and an impossible-travel session pair for the user.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-ITDR-0008 raise an account-takeover incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `ITDR-009 Sign-In Auth-Velocity and New-ASN Deviation from Learned Identity Baseline` fires.
ABIOC `ITDR-009 Impossible-Travel Geo-Velocity Deviation from Learned Sign-In Baseline` fires.
Correlation CR-ITDR-0008 raises one stitched account-takeover incident.

preventive_controls: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkeys) and conditional-access policies that bind sessions to compliant devices so stolen passwords alone cannot complete a sign-in.
Harden the help-desk identity-verification and MFA-reset workflow against the social engineering Scattered Spider and Storm-0501 use to seed valid credentials.
Continuously evaluate sign-in risk (new ASN, impossible travel, token anomalies) and revoke sessions on a step-up failure rather than at password entry only.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-identity sign-in ASN/geo/cadence baseline rather than hand-authoring static IP or geo-fence rules.
Alert on a successful sign-in from an autonomous system absent from the account's learned baseline.
Alert on two successful sign-ins from distant geographies inside a travel-impossibility window and stitch the velocity and geo deviations into one account-takeover incident.
